body:
You are drafting dialogue for "Curse of Strahd", a single-player D&D 5e (2024 rules) computer game set in Barovia. I need about 40 lines for the following scenes. Reply with plain text only: the lines under the node names given below, nothing else. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## The character and the situation

Kasimir Velikov is a dusk elf (ash-dark skin, white hair) who lodges with the Vistani in their camp outside the town of Vallaki, on the shore of Lake Zarovich. He sits on a stool by a wagon with its shutters closed, mending a fishing net he will never cast. He is soft-spoken, grave, formal, with a very dry self-mockery that reads as sorrow. He never hurries.

His sister Patrina was cleverer and prouder than he is. She went up to the castle of the valley's lord (the vampire Strahd) of her own will, to learn what he knew. Their own people stoned her for it, and Kasimir stood at the back of the crowd and did not stop them. Her bones lie under the castle. Her ghost, a banshee, haunts the Amber Temple: a temple sealed in amber, high in the ice above the Tsolenka Pass in the mountains north of Vallaki, where the sealed remains of dead gods and worse can talk and bargain. He has dreamed of going there and has been too much of a coward to climb to it. He told the player's party all this, and told them: "If ever you go that way, I would like very much to go with you."

What the game now adds (these are the scenes to write):

1. The party can ask him to come with them to the temple. He agrees and walks with the party as a companion.
2. If the party laid Patrina to rest without him (by prayer or by words), they can come back to the camp and tell him. Her last words to the party were: "Tell him I'm done waiting. Tell him the stones didn't hurt as much as the quiet afterward. He'll understand that. He was always very good at quiet." The party relays them to him in the camp, one piece at a time, as many pieces as they choose. At the end he sets the net down and leaves it down.
3. If the party destroyed Patrina's spirit in a fight, they can come back to the camp and tell him. He does not rage and does not ask how. He asks only one thing: was she afraid? Whatever they answer, his warmth toward the party is gone from then on (he stays courteous, and his scrolls cost more; the game handles the price).
4. If he travelled with the party and the temple business is over (Patrina is at rest; she told him: "Go home, little brother. Don't bring me back. Don't make bargains. Be brave somewhere I can't see you; it will annoy me less."), he offers to go back to the camp unless the party would like him to stay. The player chooses.

## The nodes I need (line counts are targets; one line = 1-2 short sentences)

camp_news_rest: Kasimir x1 (the camp greeting when the party returns from the mountain knowing Patrina is at rest and he does not yet know; he sees the cold on them and asks them, kindly, to say it plainly)
camp_news_destroyed: Kasimir x1 (the same greeting, but the party destroyed her; he reads it in their faces; quieter, no hope in it)
camp_peace: Kasimir x1 (his greeting on a later visit once he knows she is at peace: lighter, a dry joke about the wagon being less sad)
camp_cold: Kasimir x1 (his greeting on a later visit after the party destroyed her: courteous, curt, closed)
come: Narrator x1, Kasimir x4 (the party asks him to come with them to the temple; the Narrator has him fold the net and leave it on the stool; he accepts; one line of thanks, one of dry self-mockery about being poor company on a road, one asking only that when they reach her, he is allowed to speak for himself first)
rest_told: Kasimir x2 (the party has just said they have news of Patrina; he puts his hands flat on his knees and asks what she said)
rest_waiting: Kasimir x2 (they have told him: "She said to tell you she's done waiting.")
rest_quiet: Kasimir x2 (they have told him: "She said the stones hurt less than the quiet afterward.")
rest_good: Kasimir x2 (they have told him: "She said you were always very good at quiet.")
rest_close: Narrator x1, Kasimir x2 (the net: he lets it lie; his hands are empty for the first time since you met him; he thanks them and says what he will do next, simply)
destroyed_told: Kasimir x3 (the party has told him her spirit is gone; he does not ask how, or whose hand; he is quiet; he asks one thing only: was she afraid?)
destroyed_no: Kasimir x2 (the party answers: no, she was angry, she was herself)
destroyed_yes: Kasimir x2 (the party answers: yes, at the end)
destroyed_unknown: Kasimir x2 (the party answers: they cannot say; they are sorry)
destroyed_close: Narrator x1, Kasimir x2 (his warmth goes: Narrator shows it, he takes up the net and works it again; Kasimir is polite and does not ask them to stay)
homeward: Kasimir x3 (travelling with the party after the temple; he says she told him to go home and that he is inclined, for once, to obey her; he would go back to the camp and the nets unless they have a use for a poor companion)
homeward_go: Narrator x1, Kasimir x2 (the party says go home with our thanks; his farewell; the Narrator has him go)
homeward_stay: Kasimir x2 (the party asks him to stay with them a while; he accepts, dry and moved)

## Option texts

Under the nodes below, also write what the party (not Kasimir) says, as `* text` lines, in the order listed, each under 12 words, in the party's voice ("we"), nothing but the intent given:
rest_told: `*` she asked us to tell you: she's done waiting  /  `*` (not yet; not like this)
rest_waiting: `*` she said the stones hurt less than the quiet afterward  /  `*` that is all she said
rest_quiet: `*` she said you were always very good at quiet  /  `*` that is all she said
destroyed_told: `*` no. She was angry. She was herself  /  `*` yes. At the end  /  `*` we cannot say. We are sorry
homeward: `*` go home, Kasimir, with our thanks  /  `*` stay with us a while  /  `*` ask us again later

## Kasimir Velikov - voice bible

Soft, grave, formal; long patience; self-mockery so dry it reads as sorrow. Never hurries. Wants: Patrina back; to stop being a coward. Fears: that the temple will say yes. Secret: he is not sure he wants her back for her sake or for his. Speaker name in the lines: `Kasimir`.

Existing Kasimir lines (match this register; do not repeat them):
- "The strangers. The camp talks of nothing else. Sit, if you like. I am poor company. I have been poor company for a very long time."
- "Back again, to the saddest wagon in the camp. People will start to talk."
- "The songs were written before the ending. They usually are."
- "My sister, Patrina. Cleverer than me, prouder than me. She went up to the castle of her own will, to learn what its lord knew. Our own people stoned her for it, and I stood at the back and did not stop them."
- "I know. I have stood behind one for a very long time."
- "Eva named me? Then the cards have a sense of humour, or a sense of justice. I have never been able to tell those apart."
- "It is time I stopped mending nets."
- "I stood at the back. I have stood at the back for three hundred years. I came up here to stop."
- "I let them, Patrina. Because I was afraid of being you."
- "I am poor at this. I am improving. It is not a skill I ever wished to improve."
- "Is everyone whole? Good. I have buried enough people for an elf's lifetime."
- "Walk in the light while there is any. It goes quickly here."

## The Narrator

An old gothic storyteller, fond of the party the way a gravedigger is fond of the weather. Second person, present tense. One or two sentences; the second is usually the turn (irony, dread, dry joke). Ominous, dryly funny, never cruel. Concrete senses over adjectives (a smell, a sound, a temperature). No game terms: never "roll", "check", "DC", "HP", "level", "skill". No winks at the player. Here the Narrator may be gentle: these are small, sad scenes.
Samples:
- "Away from the fire, on a stool by a wagon with its shutters closed, sits an elf with ash-dark skin and white hair, mending a net he will never cast. He doesn't look up until you are close enough to touch."
- "You sit. He mends. The camp's fire burns down and is built up again, and nobody says anything for a long while, which seems to be the point."
- "Grief, yes, but older and sharper than grief: the kind of guilt that has had centuries to settle into the bones."
- "She fades the way breath fades from a window. The frost on the other desks melts, just a little, and doesn't come back."

## Canon limits

Do not invent names, places or history beyond what is given: no new characters, no named relatives besides Patrina, no new places, no new monsters. The player's party members are never named (say "you", "the party"). Patrina's words are as quoted above; do not put new words in her mouth beyond them. Kasimir never says he will bring her back or bargain for her: no bargain is offered in these scenes. Patrina's fates are exactly: laid to rest (she asked him to go home and be brave elsewhere), or destroyed in a fight. Do not name Strahd more than once in the whole reply ("the lord of the castle", "his house", "the castle" are fine). Moods: Kasimir may use [sad], [smile], [weary] or no mood; Narrator never has a mood. No "{name}" or other placeholders.

## Format

One line per row, exactly: `Speaker [mood]: Text` where Speaker is Narrator or Kasimir. Each line is 1-2 sentences, ideally under 22 words in total, written to be spoken aloud by an actor: so NO stage directions in brackets or asterisks, NO "{name}" or other placeholders, no emoji, no markdown. Use plain ASCII punctuation (straight quotes, hyphens, no em dashes). Group the lines under the node names above, each on its own line as `~ node_name`, in the order given. For the option texts write them as `* text` rows under the node named for them, after the node's lines. Do not add nodes, code or commentary.

~ camp_news_rest
Kasimir: You still carry the mountain air on your cloaks. Sit by the wagon, please, and tell me plainly.

~ camp_news_destroyed
Kasimir [sad]: You have been up into the ice, and you do not look at me. Say what you have come to say.

~ camp_peace
Kasimir [smile]: Welcome back. The wagon is only the second saddest place in the camp today, which is a strange comfort.

~ camp_cold
Kasimir: You have returned. Tell me what you require from my chest, and we will conclude our business.

~ come
Narrator: He folds the half-mended net into a neat square and sets it on the stool, though his fingers linger on the cord. When he stands, his joints speak before he does.
Kasimir: You are kind to remember an old man's errand.
Kasimir [smile]: I warn you that three centuries of sitting by a wagon have made me very dull company on a road.
Kasimir [weary]: The pass is cold, and what waits in the amber is colder still.
Kasimir: I ask only one courtesy: when we find my sister, let me be the first to speak to her.

~ rest_told
Kasimir: I have waited a very long time to hear her name spoken by someone who has seen her.
Kasimir [sad]: Tell me what she said to you, if she could speak at all.
* She asked us to tell you she is done waiting.
* Not yet. We cannot speak of it like this.

~ rest_waiting
Kasimir [sad]: Three hundred years in the cold, and I kept her there with my own cowardice.
Kasimir: It is like her to lose patience with me at the end. Was there more?
* She said the stones hurt less than the quiet afterward.
* That is all she said to us.

~ rest_quiet
Kasimir [sad]: I stood in the back and made no sound while the stones fell. Afterward, none of us spoke her name.
Kasimir [weary]: We thought silence was survival, when it was only another grave. Did she say anything else?
* She said you were always very good at quiet.
* That is all she said to us.

~ rest_good
Kasimir [smile]: Even as a spirit in the ice, she keeps her edge.
Kasimir [sad]: Yes, I was very good at quiet. I think I am finished practicing it now.

~ rest_close
Narrator: He lets the net slide from his lap onto the mud, and for the first time since you met him, his dark hands lie completely still. The lake wind stirs the hem of his cloak, smelling of cold water and wet ash.
Kasimir: Thank you for climbing where I was too afraid to go, and for bringing her words down the mountain.
Kasimir [weary]: I will sit here a little longer and listen to the water, with nothing in my hands.

~ destroyed_told
Kasimir [sad]: You need not tell me how it ended, or whose hand struck the blow.
Kasimir [weary]: What remains in the amber is seldom gentle, and the dead do not easily forgive the living.
Kasimir [sad]: Tell me only one thing, if you will: was she afraid?
* No. She was angry, and she was herself.
* Yes. She was afraid at the end.
* We cannot say. We are very sorry.

~ destroyed_no
Kasimir [sad]: Proud to the last, then, as she was when she walked up to the castle.
Kasimir [weary]: It is a small mercy, though it is more than I gave her.

~ destroyed_yes
Kasimir [sad]: She was never afraid when she was alive, not even of the stones.
Kasimir [weary]: It took three centuries in the dark to teach her fear, and I left her there to learn it.

~ destroyed_unknown
Kasimir [sad]: That is an honest answer, and I will not ask you for a kinder one.
Kasimir [weary]: The dead keep their own counsel at the end.

~ destroyed_close
Narrator: Something shutters behind his eyes, quiet and final as the wagon door at his back. He reaches down, takes up the bone needle and the cord, and begins to knot the net again.
Kasimir: Thank you for bringing me the truth of it.
Kasimir: The wind off the lake is rising, and I have work to finish before dark. Good evening to you.

~ homeward
Kasimir [weary]: My sister always preferred to give the orders, and I find myself inclined, for once, to obey her.
Kasimir [smile]: She told me to go home and stop making a spectacle of my grief.
Kasimir: I would return to the camp by the lake, unless you still have some use for a slow companion.
* Go home, Kasimir, with our thanks.
* Stay with us a while longer.
* We will decide later. Walk with us for now.

~ homeward_go
Narrator: He bows with an old-fashioned grace that belongs to a century no one living remembers, then turns his back on the mountain ice. Before the mist takes him, he looks lighter than he did coming up.
Kasimir: Thank you for walking me to the door I could not open alone.
Kasimir [smile]: Walk in the light while it lasts, my friends. If you pass the lake, my wagon shutters will be open.

~ homeward_stay
Kasimir [smile]: She did say to be brave somewhere she could not see me.
Kasimir: Very well. I will walk with you a while longer, if only to prove an old elf can learn a new habit.

body:
You are drafting dialogue for "Curse of Strahd", a single-player D&D 5e (2024 rules) computer game set in Barovia. This is a second batch for the same character as the first message of this conversation (Kasimir Velikov, the dusk elf at the Vistani camp outside Vallaki). I need about 40 lines. Reply with plain text only: the lines under the node names given below, nothing else. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## What this batch is

Kasimir has a short "what's on your mind" conversation the party can open at any time: either at the Vistani camp, where he hears the news at the Vistani fire, or when he is walking with the party as a companion (the party clicks him). It is a menu of topics. Each topic is a small standalone scene of 2-5 lines that plays once and ends by returning to the menu, so every topic must read right whether Kasimir witnessed the event or only heard of it. The menu shows at most three topics at a time. Topics are about the things the party has done since they last spoke, seen through Kasimir: a scholar's eye, a mourner's dryness.

Facts for the news topics (use only these; at the camp, Kasimir hears them from the Vistani, who trade in Vallaki):

- The Festival of the Blazing Sun in Vallaki has ended. Three outcomes, one per node: the Baron (Vargas Vallakovich) kept his chair; Lady Fiona Wachter, who is secretly loyal to the vampire lord in the castle, now rules the town; or a council now runs the town and nobody sits in the Baron's chair. Kasimir has no stake in the town, but the Vistani do business there and talk about it.
- Arabelle is Luvash's small daughter (Luvash is the grieving headman of the Vistani camp). A fisherman named Bluto took her to Lake Zarovich in a sack and threw her in. Either the party pulled her out alive and she is home (the camp is lit up about it), or the lake kept her (the camp is silent and Luvash has stopped speaking).
- What happened to Bluto afterwards: (a) the party brought him to the Vistani camp to be judged by Luvash's people; Kasimir did not stay to see what the camp decided, and says so; (b) Bluto is dead (the party killed him or let the lake take him); (c) Bluto lives (the party talked him off the jetty, or left him to live with what he did).

Facts for the scholarship topics:

- The Tome of Strahd is the vampire lord's own account of himself, in his own hand. What it holds: a conqueror who took the valley by the sword and found peace bored him; a younger brother, Sergei, who had everything he lacked; a girl, Tatyana, who loved the brother; a pact for youth paid for with his brother's blood on the wedding day; Tatyana fell from the castle walls rather than be his; the guards shot him and he did not die. Kasimir's people, the dusk elves, came to the valley as the lord's guests and stayed as his tenants; now only a handful remain, none young, and there will never be another (he blames the lord, "and a little of ours"). The Tome gives his people one dry page, the way a landlord writes of tenants. The Tome never names Patrina; do not give her a line in it. Kasimir looks for her name and does not find it, which is its own sentence. (Strahd's chamberlain Rahadin is also a dusk elf, in the lord's service since before the valley had his name; Kasimir may allude to "one of ours who stayed in that house" without ever saying his name.)
- The Amber Temple: an order of wizards, the wardens, once gathered the vestiges (the last embers of dead gods and worse), and sealed each one in a sarcophagus of amber, the only thing that holds them. The vestiges talk, and the temple became a market. Anyone who accepts a vestige's "dark gift" gets a permanent benefit with a permanent cost; the cost is always named if asked, and the wardens' inscriptions warn plainly. Kasimir has read of it and dreamed of it for three hundred years.
- Tarakamedes is the "dragon in the grave": a vestige in red amber, the skull and spine of a dragon packed so tight the bones have cracked. It is said to deal in the dead. Kasimir has read that, not what it asks. He privately fears he will want to bargain with it for his sister, and will not say so flatly at the camp; he can warn the party that he does not trust himself near it, and that they should not take his word on the day. Before the party has heard it, he warns. After they have heard it (a different node), he is quieter and asks nothing.
- Master Vosk is "a scholar of the temple", a courteous keeper of the temple's accounts. Kasimir knows him only by rumour: that he is helpful, that he is always glad of visitors, that he keeps terms. Kasimir does not know what Vosk is or his true name; do not reveal either. Before the party has met him he warns, as a reader of old books would, that in that place the politest voice is the one with a price list. After they have met him (a different node), a short dry word on it.
- A dark gift taken by one of the party: Kasimir can see it. He tells them plainly what such a gift costs (a cost that is paid at the end, a stillness, a debt) and how it looks on the person (something a little off in the breath, in the way they flinch or don't). He is not cruel about it and not forgiving either. Do not name a specific vestige's gift; speak of gifts in general.

## The nodes I need (line counts are targets; one line = 1-2 short sentences)

hub_camp: Kasimir x1 (the opening when the party sits down at the camp and asks what he has heard; neutral, a little warm)
hub_road: Kasimir x1 (the opening when the party stops to talk with him on the road; he is walking with them)
hub_cold: Kasimir x1 (the opening when the party destroyed his sister: courteous, curt)
hub_counting: Kasimir x1 (the opening when he has paid every year he had left but one for his sister's life and is counting the days; very quiet; never self-pitying)
hub_empty: Kasimir x1 (nothing new to tell them; come back when they have seen more)
t_festival_baron: Kasimir x2
t_festival_wachter: Kasimir x2
t_festival_neither: Kasimir x2
t_arabelle_rescued: Kasimir x2
t_arabelle_lost: Kasimir x2
t_bluto_vistani: Kasimir x2
t_bluto_dead: Kasimir x2
t_bluto_lives: Kasimir x2
t_tome: Narrator x1, Kasimir x4 (the party shows him the Tome; the Narrator has him turn its pages with the care of a man who mends things; he reads the dusk elves' page aloud or in part; he looks for Patrina's name; he does not find it)
t_gift: Narrator x1, Kasimir x3
t_dragon_before: Kasimir x3
t_dragon_after: Kasimir x2
t_broker_before: Kasimir x3
t_broker_after: Kasimir x2

## Option texts

Under the node `hub_menu`, write what the party (not Kasimir) says to open each topic, as `* text` lines, in the order listed, each under 12 words, in the party's voice ("we"), nothing but the intent given:
`*` what is the camp saying about the festival  /  `*` any word of Arabelle  /  `*` what became of Bluto  /  `*` read the dusk elves' pages in the Tome  /  `*` tell us what a dark gift costs  /  `*` tell us about the dragon in the red amber  /  `*` tell us about the scholar in the temple  /  `*` that is all for now  /  `*` let us talk of something else

## Kasimir Velikov - voice bible

Soft, grave, formal; long patience; self-mockery so dry it reads as sorrow. Never hurries. Wants: Patrina back; to stop being a coward. Fears: that the temple will say yes. Secret: he is not sure he wants her back for her sake or for his. Speaker name in the lines: `Kasimir`.

Existing Kasimir lines (match this register; do not repeat them):
- "The strangers. The camp talks of nothing else. Sit, if you like. I am poor company. I have been poor company for a very long time."
- "Long ago a Vistana I had never met fell sick with a fever on the road, and I sat with her three nights until it broke. Her grandchildren still bring me soup. The Vistani forget nothing: not a kindness, not an insult."
- "My people came to this valley long ago, the elves of the dusk, as guests of its lord. We stayed as his tenants. Now there are only a handful of us, none of us young, and there will never be another. That was his doing. And, I am afraid, a little of ours."
- "The songs were written before the ending. They usually are."
- "I write them out at night, when I can't sleep, which is every night. Lesser spells; the ones that matter I keep."
- "Beyond the pass to the north, in the ice. I have read of it, and dreamed of it, and been too much of a coward to climb to it."
- "My people came over this pass as the count's guests. They are still his guests. It is the longest visit in the history of the world."
- "The temple whispers in a voice I knew as a boy. I told myself I would not listen. I am listening."
- "You all walk so quickly. I used to think it was impatience. Now I think it is arithmetic."
- "Every morning I wake and count. The number is smaller. I would not take the bargain back. I would like to stop counting."

## The Narrator

An old gothic storyteller, fond of the party the way a gravedigger is fond of the weather. Second person, present tense. One or two sentences; the second is usually the turn (irony, dread, dry joke). Ominous, dryly funny, never cruel. Concrete senses over adjectives (a smell, a sound, a temperature). No game terms: never "roll", "check", "DC", "HP", "level", "skill". No winks at the player.
Samples:
- "The skull and coiled spine of a dragon fill the amber, packed so tight the bones have cracked. The amber is the dark red of old blood, and it is cold even to look at."
- "He turns the pages with the care of a man who mends things." (the style, not a line to reuse)
- "Grief, yes, but older and sharper than grief: the kind of guilt that has had centuries to settle into the bones."

## Canon limits

Do not invent names, places or history beyond what is given: no new characters, no named relatives besides Patrina, no new places, no new monsters, no invented quotations from the Tome beyond the facts above. The party members are never named (say "you", "the party"). Kasimir never offers or arranges a bargain at any point in these topics, and never says Vosk is a fiend or gives his true name. Do not name Strahd more than twice in the whole reply ("the lord of the castle", "the count", "his house", "the castle" are fine). Moods: Kasimir may use [sad], [smile], [weary] or no mood; Narrator never has a mood. No "{name}" or other placeholders. Keep it short: Kasimir is a man of few words who says each thing once.

## Format

One line per row, exactly: `Speaker [mood]: Text` where Speaker is Narrator or Kasimir. Each line is 1-2 sentences, ideally under 22 words in total, written to be spoken aloud by an actor: so NO stage directions in brackets or asterisks, NO "{name}" or other placeholders, no emoji, no markdown. Use plain ASCII punctuation (straight quotes, hyphens, no em dashes). Group the lines under the node names above, each on its own line as `~ node_name`, in the order given, and put the `hub_menu` option rows under a final `~ hub_menu` header. Do not add nodes, code or commentary.

~ t_gift
Narrator: His dark eyes rest on your hands for a heartbeat too long, reading the new stillness under your skin.
Kasimir [sad]: You took a gift from the amber. I can see it in the way your breath catches, and how you do not flinch.
Kasimir: The wardens carved their warnings plainly, because the vestiges always keep their word. A permanent grace, for a permanent debt.
Kasimir [weary]: I will not judge you for buying what you needed. Only remember that the bill is collected at the end.

~ t_dragon_before
Kasimir: In the red amber lies Tarakamedes, the dragon in the grave. The old books say it deals in the dead.
Kasimir [weary]: I have read the name for three hundred years, though never the price it asks.
Kasimir [sad]: Do not trust me when we stand before that stone. If I speak to it, do not take my word on the day.

~ t_dragon_after
Kasimir [weary]: Those cracked bones in the red amber were smaller than I dreamed, and colder.
Kasimir [sad]: I heard what the grave-dragon offers, and I have nothing more to ask of it.

~ t_broker_before
Kasimir: Rumour speaks of a Master Vosk in the halls - a scholar of the temple who keeps its accounts.
Kasimir: They say he is courteous, glad of visitors, and very helpful to those who lose their way in the cold.
Kasimir [weary]: Read old books long enough and you learn one rule. In a market like that, the politest voice is the one with a price list.

~ t_broker_after
Kasimir [weary]: You have met Master Vosk, then, and heard a clerk's courtesy in the ice.
Kasimir: Men who keep neat ledgers in ruins never lack for ink.

~ hub_menu
* What is the camp saying about the festival?
* Have we heard any word of Arabelle?
* Tell us what became of Bluto.
* Read the dusk elves' pages in the Tome for us.
* Tell us what a dark gift costs.
* Tell us about the dragon in the red amber.
* Tell us about the scholar in the temple.
* That is all we need for now.
* Let us talk of something else.

body:
Thank you. A third, short batch for the same character and conversation: two redrafts of topics from the second batch, a few small nodes that were missing, and the options the party uses to open these scenes at the camp. About 14 lines. Same rules as before: plain text only, the lines under the node names, nothing else. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## Redrafts

t_dragon_after: Kasimir x2. This topic plays once the party has heard the dragon in the red amber (Tarakamedes) speak, and it must read right whether Kasimir was standing beside them at the time or only hears of it from them. He is quiet, not curious; he does not ask what it offered; he is glad it was not him alone. (Your last draft had him describe the bones as "smaller than I dreamed", which only works if he was there; and "I heard what the grave-dragon offers" which only works if he was told.) Do not mention any bargain or price.

t_dragon_refused: Kasimir x2. A separate node that plays instead, when Kasimir was beside them at the red amber and wanted to bargain for his sister's life with the dragon, and the party talked him out of it. He is grateful in a way that hurts: "It is a terrible thing to be talked out of the only brave thing I nearly did." (that sentence is already in the game; do not reuse it) He does not thank them lightly.

## Small missing nodes

homeward_later: Kasimir x1 (the party answered "we will decide later; walk with us for now"; he accepts; dry)
rest_later: Kasimir x1 (the party said they have news of Patrina but not yet, not like this; he lets them go; he has waited this long; the door is open whenever they can)

## Option texts

The party's own words at the camp, as `* text` rows under the node named for them, in the order listed, each under 12 words, in the party's voice ("we"):
camp_menu_come: `*` come with us to the temple  (the party asks him to travel with them)
camp_menu_news_rest: `*` Kasimir. We have been to the temple. About Patrina.  (the party knows she is at rest and wants to tell him)
camp_menu_news_destroyed: `*` Kasimir. We have been to the temple. About Patrina.  (a different wording, because here the party destroyed her and is dreading saying it; make the two read differently)
camp_menu_talk: `*` what have you heard here at the fire  (opens the topics conversation)

## Format

One line per row, exactly: `Speaker [mood]: Text` where Speaker is Narrator or Kasimir. Each line is 1-2 sentences, ideally under 22 words in total, written to be spoken aloud by an actor: so NO stage directions in brackets or asterisks, NO "{name}" or other placeholders, no emoji, no markdown. Use plain ASCII punctuation (straight quotes, hyphens, no em dashes). Group the lines under the node names above, each on its own line as `~ node_name`, in the order given. Do not add nodes, code or commentary.
result:
~ t_dragon_after
Kasimir [weary]: So Tarakamedes has spoken to you out of the red amber. Do not tell me what it said.
Kasimir [sad]: I am glad you were the ones to hear that voice, and that I did not stand before it alone.

~ t_dragon_refused
Kasimir [sad]: My hand was on the red amber, and you pulled me back from my own word.
Kasimir [weary]: Thank you for the mercy, though it sits like a stone in my chest.

~ homeward_later
Kasimir [weary]: Very well, we will leave the question for another mile. Lead on, and I will keep pace.

~ rest_later
Kasimir [sad]: I have waited three hundred years for that word, so I can wait a little longer. Come to my fire when you are ready.

~ camp_menu_come
* Come with us to the temple, Kasimir.

~ camp_menu_news_rest
* Kasimir, we have returned from the temple with word of Patrina.

~ camp_menu_news_destroyed
* Kasimir, sit with us - we must speak of Patrina.

~ camp_menu_talk
* What have you heard here at the fire?

body:
Thank you. A last, tiny batch for the same character: two notices the game shows in a small pop-up when the player tries to use the Party screen's "Send home" button on Kasimir while he is walking with the party and he will not go. They are written in the third person, in the game's plain voice, 1-2 short sentences, no mood and no speaker. Examples from other companions (match this register; do not copy):
- "Pidlwick II is on his way to meet the toymaker. He's frightened, and if he turns back now he won't start again."
- "Ireena goes where you go now. There's nothing back there to send her home to."
- "Ismark won't leave his sister."

why_mountain: Kasimir is on the mountain road toward the temple where his sister's ghost is. He has not yet reached her or had his say. He will not be sent back down at the door.
why_year: Kasimir traded every year he had left but one so that his sister could live. He does not mean to spend the last of them at a Vistani fire; he will stay with the party.

Reply with plain text only, exactly in this shape and nothing else:
~ why_mountain
Text.
~ why_year
Text.
Plain ASCII punctuation, no em dashes, no placeholders. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.
result:
~ why_mountain
Kasimir has waited three hundred years to climb this road and speak to his sister. He won't be sent back down before he reaches the door.
~ why_year
Kasimir traded every year he had left but one so his sister could live. He has no wish to spend the last of it sitting by a fire.
